title: Wave Behavior
learning_goal: Investigate reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference, standing waves, Doppler effect, polarization, and superposition.

stages.title: 1. Reflection and refraction
stages.content: Reflection occurs when a wave bounces from a boundary. Refraction occurs when a wave changes speed and direction as it enters a different medium.

stages.title: 2. Diffraction
stages.content: Diffraction is the spreading of waves around edges or through openings. It is strongest when the opening or obstacle size is comparable to the wavelength.

stages.title: 3. Interference and superposition
stages.content: When waves overlap, their displacements add. Constructive interference increases amplitude, while destructive interference reduces amplitude.

stages.title: 4. Standing waves and resonance
stages.content: Standing waves form from interference between waves traveling in opposite directions. Nodes have minimal motion and antinodes have maximum motion.

stages.title: 5. Doppler effect and polarization
stages.content: The Doppler effect is an observed frequency shift caused by relative motion between source and observer. Polarization restricts the orientation of transverse-wave oscillations.

stages.title: 6. Guided practice
stages.prompt: Two identical wave pulses meet crest-to-crest. What type of interference occurs?
stages.hint: Ask whether their displacements add or cancel.
stages.alternate_explanation: Two upward displacements combine into a larger upward displacement.

stages.title: 7. Mastery check
stages.content: To demonstrate mastery, distinguish major wave behaviors, predict interference outcomes, identify nodes and antinodes, explain Doppler shifts, and describe polarization.
